layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The entire area of Manipur is a Protected Area (Third Schedule, Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025). Every foreigner needs a Protected Area Permit to enter or stay. The Ministry of Home Affairs withdrew the 2010 exemption for Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland with immediate effect on 17 December 2024. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (e-FRRO) or the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; permits are electronic only. Indian missions advise getting approval 30 days ahead if applying with the visa, or applying to the FRRO at least 15 days ahead if already in India. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there, need the central government's prior approval.

Manipur's Inner Line Permit is for Indian citizens from outside the state, under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation 1873 as extended to Manipur in 2019. It isn't the permit foreigners need; foreigners use the Protected Area Permit above.

layers.authority: Foreigners Registration Officer of the state or district
layers.process: Every foreigner visiting Manipur, Mizoram or Nagaland must register with the state or district Foreigners Registration Officer within 24 hours of arrival (MHA letter of 17 December 2024).

sources.title: Protected Area Permit / Restricted Area Permit
sources.supports: all of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Sikkim need PAP/RAP; e-FRRO only; approvals 30 days ahead with the visa, or 15 days ahead to the FRRO if already in India; Bhutan citizens exempt (read via a search-index snapshot)

zone-requirements.note: Settled 3 November 2026: a Protected Area Permit is required. The MHA letter of 17 December 2024 withdrew the exemption, and the Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025 lists the whole state. Smartraveller's line that the state is temporarily excluded is out of date (it still links the older MHA FAQ, which describes the 2010 exemption). Nagaland's Dimapur district page confirms the withdrawal (it gives March 2025 as the start for Nagaland).

laws.rule: The whole of Manipur is a Protected Area: a foreigner must hold a permit to enter or stay. The civil authority can attach conditions, including reporting to police and limits on surveying, sketching or photography.
